findings.issue_text: [BUG] The `.names a` rule transposes both lightness values: the light-theme branch jumps from 30% to 70% and the dark-theme branch receives 30% instead of the 70% that the mechanical 100−L transform used at every other site in this diff. In the default light theme the bold usernames in the `.names` panel render approximately #bdbdbd on white — effectively invisible — and in dark themes they render approximately #646464 on the ~#222 background, dimmer than every other muted element in the same file, so the rule ships broken in both themes.

[BUG] `.custom-message-length` swaps both branches relative to its previous 70% value and to its desktop twin in desktop/modal.scss:94, which keeps 70% light / 30% dark; mobile now emits 30% for light themes and 70% for dark. Mobile light-theme users see the modal character-counter hint in dark ~#656565 instead of the muted light gray the desktop modal still shows for the identical element, so the same component renders with different prominence on mobile vs desktop, and the light-theme change falls outside the PR's dark-theme-only contract.

[BUG] The section h3's light-theme value is changed from 20% to 50% lightness, violating the keep-the-light-branch pattern applied everywhere else and diverging from the parallel desktop h3 (desktop/topic-post.scss:321), which keeps 20% light / 80% dark. In light themes the same heading renders near-black on desktop but mid-gray on mobile, and on mobile the h3 now equals the adjacent h4 (also 50/50 at line 189), flattening the heading hierarchy desktop preserves; dark-theme values diverge from the desktop rendering as well.

[ADVISORY] The profile-header `.name` rule silently changes its light-theme value from 30% to 50% (and its dark branch to 50% instead of 70%), an out-of-scope light-theme change in a PR that only claims to fix dark themes. Light-theme users see the real-name text roughly twice as light as before with no stated rationale, and the parallel `.name` rules in common/base/user.scss keep the old 30%-based pair, so rules for the same element concept now disagree; if this is not a deliberate design tweak it is the same transcription-error class as the swapped pairs elsewhere in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The mobile profile `.name` rule silently changes its light-theme value from 30% to 50% (dark branch 50 instead of 70), out of scope for a dark-theme-only fix. Light-theme mobile users see the profile real-name dimmed relative to its previous value with no stated intent; it mirrors the desktop twin (desktop/user.scss:522) so it may be deliberate, but it contradicts the PR contract and disagrees with the unchanged 30%-based `.name` in common/base/user.scss.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-replicates the two-literal pattern dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, L%), scale-color($secondary, (100−L)%)) at roughly 90 sites instead of deriving the complement once in a helper, even though the codebase already abstracts per-theme percentage pairs via dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, light%, dark%). Every future lightness sweep must hand-maintain ~90 complement pairs, and this very diff mis-transcribes five of them (three shipped as wrong values — the `.names a`, `.custom-message-length`, and mobile h3 findings), so the next edit of this class will drift again and reviewers cannot mechanically verify the paired literals; a single-argument helper would collapse each pair to one number.

[BUG] The conversion applies the (70%, 30%) lightness pair to a line whose original value was 30%, silently changing the light-scheme branch from scale-color($primary, 30%) to scale-color($primary, 70%) instead of preserving it. Light-scheme users see this bold link (beside the .arrow glyph in the replies/gap indicator block) fade from a 30% tint to a 70% tint (~1.9:1 on white), and dark-scheme users get scale-color($secondary, 30%) — only 30% lighter than the page background — so the link becomes near-unreadable in both theme families; every other original-30% site in this diff (e.g. common/base/user.scss:119) correctly keeps 30% light / 70% dark, proving this site's branches are swapped.

[BUG] The mobile .custom-message-length color is converted to scale-color($primary, 30%) for light schemes and scale-color($secondary, 70%) for dark schemes — the exact inverse of its original 70% value and of the desktop twin at desktop/modal.scss:94 which uses 70% light / 30% dark. Light-scheme mobile users see the custom-message character counter change from a subtle 70% tint to near-black, while dark-scheme mobile users see it rendered at a 70%-lightened secondary (bright gray) instead of desktop's 30%, so the identical component renders with opposite prominence on mobile versus desktop in both theme families.

[BUG] The mobile onebox h3 conversion rewrites the original 20% tint as 50% in both branches, diverging from the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss:320 which correctly preserves 20% light / 80% dark for the same heading. Light-scheme mobile onebox headings drop from a 20% tint to a 50% tint (roughly half the contrast for the primary content heading of every onebox), and dark-scheme mobile headings render at 50% instead of the 80% desktop uses, so onebox titles go visibly dim on mobile in both theme families.

[BUG] The user-card .name conversion changes the light-scheme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it, and uses 50% for the dark branch where the same-named element on the profile page (common/base/user.scss:124, converted in this same diff) keeps 30% light / 70% dark. Light-scheme users see full names on user cards lose contrast (30%→50% tint) with no dark-theme-related justification, and dark-scheme users see names dimmer than the 70% complement used for every other 30%-tinted element — a silent light-theme visual change shipped in a PR titled as dark-theme-only.

[BUG] The mobile user-card .name conversion changes the light-scheme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it, and uses 50% for the dark branch instead of the 70% complement used for the same element on the profile page (common/base/user.scss:124). Mobile user cards render the full name at a 50% tint in light schemes (previously 30%, lower contrast against the adjacent bold username) and at 50% in dark schemes instead of 70%, so names fade on both breakpoints and both theme families while the profile-page twin keeps its original styling.

[ADVISORY] The diff converts the disabled-state backgrounds of #reply-title and .wmd-input but leaves the sibling active-state text color darken($primary, 40%) two lines below unconverted, dropping the composer input text itself from the dark-theme fix. Dark-scheme mobile users composing a post see textarea text at a 40%-darkened primary (mid-gray, ~4:1 contrast) while every adjacent rule in the same block was corrected, so the PR's dark-theme readability goal silently skips the one element users type into.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-writes ~118 dark-light-choose complement pairs across 32 stylesheets with no verification of any kind — no lint rule against bare scale-color($primary, no compiled light-scheme CSS snapshot — for the light-scheme-unchanged acceptance criterion its own title implies. That unenforced criterion is already violated at five sites in this very diff (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497) and nothing catches them — the desktop/mobile twin copies of shared components even drifted in opposite directions — so the remaining unconverted siblings (e.g. darken($primary, 40%) at mobile/compose.scss:174) and any follow-up sweep will repeat the same silent regressions; a single dl-scale($lightness) Sass helper or a bare-scale-color lint rule would make the entire error class impossible.

[BUG] The dark-light-choose arguments at this site are inverted against the uniform (old-lightness, 100-old-lightness) conversion the PR applies everywhere else: the light-scheme value changes from 30% to 70% lightness and the dark-scheme value becomes 30% instead of the 70% the pattern requires. Light-theme users see this bold link in the nav.post-controls block (immediately above the .arrow rule) washed out from dark gray to 70%-lightness pale gray, and dark-theme users get scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) - a dim gray instead of the 70% every parallel site in this diff uses - so the link loses prominence in both schemes; the light-scheme change is untraceable to the requirement that only dark themes switch to $secondary.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length conversion inverts the argument pair used for the identical selector on desktop (desktop/modal.scss:94 keeps (70%, 30%)): mobile's light-scheme value drops from 70% to 30% lightness and its dark-scheme value becomes 70% instead of 30%. Mobile users on light themes see the modal hint (the custom-message character counter in flag/contact-staff modals) change from subtle pale gray to near-black text, and mobile dark-theme users get a bright 70% gray where desktop shows the intended dim 30% - the same component renders with mirrored emphasis on mobile vs desktop.

[BUG] The h3 inside the a.star card block changes its light-scheme value from 20% to 50% lightness and its dark-scheme value to 50%, discarding both the previous light value and the (20%, 80%) pair the PR gives desktop's identical h3 (desktop/topic-post.scss:321). Mobile light-theme users see the card heading lose most of its contrast (near-black 20% becomes mid-gray 50%) while mobile dark-theme users get a 50% gray where desktop renders 80%, so the same heading renders differently across breakpoints; the light-scheme change is untraceable to the requirement that only dark themes switch to $secondary.

[BUG] The user-profile .name conversion changes the light-scheme value from 30% to 50% lightness, which is untraceable to the stated requirement that only dark themes switch to $secondary and off-pattern (the rule yields (30%, 70%), and the user-card .name in common/base/user.scss keeps 30%). Desktop light-theme users see the profile name lighten to the same mid-gray as .title, flattening the name/title hierarchy and splitting .name into two different light-scheme colors (profile page 50%, user card 30%) that future theme adjustments must reconcile.

[BUG] The mobile user-profile .name conversion changes the light-scheme value from 30% to 50% lightness, which is untraceable to the requirement that only dark themes switch to $secondary and off-pattern (the rule yields (30%, 70%); the user-card .name in common/base/user.scss keeps 30%). Mobile light-theme users see the profile name lighten to the same mid-gray as .title, and the profile-page .name now disagrees with the 30% user-card .name, so the same conceptual element renders with different light-scheme colors depending on where it appears.

[ADVISORY] The PR hand-writes the two-argument dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: (100-X)%)) expression roughly ninety times across thirty files with no shared SCSS helper or variable, and the hand-maintained inversion arithmetic has already drifted at five sites in this same diff (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497). The next contributor needing a muted color copy-pastes from one of the drifted sites and propagates the wrong pair, and any theme-wide contrast adjustment means re-editing ~90 call sites in 30 files; a single helper such as muted-color($pct) returning dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $pct), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $pct)) deletes the per-site arithmetic that produced all five drifts.

[BUG] The replacement for the bold username link in the replies row inverts the lightness pair: the light-theme branch silently changes from the original 30% to 70%, and the dark branch gets 30% where every sibling rule in this PR uses the 100-X complement (70%). In light (default) themes the bold usernames in the 'show replies' rows render at scale-color($primary, 70%) - near-white text on a white background, effectively invisible (previously readable 30%); in dark themes the same links render at 30% secondary, dimmer than the surrounding .post-date/.arrow rules at 40%, so both themes get a broken value in a PR whose contract is to change dark themes only.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length replacement swaps the pair relative to the convention used at ~90 other sites in this diff: the light branch changes from the original 70% to 30%, and the dark branch becomes 70% instead of 30%. In light themes the character-count hint in the modal changes from faint 70% gray to near-black 30% - an unrequested light-theme behavior change in a PR titled as a dark-theme fix - and in dark themes mobile renders the identical element at 70% (bright, high emphasis) while desktop/modal.scss:94 renders it at 30% (dim), so the same hint has opposite visual weight on mobile vs desktop.

[BUG] The mobile h3 (topic title) replacement pastes the adjacent h4 rule's 50%/50% pair instead of preserving the original 20% light value - desktop/topic-post.scss:321 converts the matching h3 correctly as 20%/80%. On light themes the mobile topic title - the most prominent text on the page - drops from near-full-strength 20% lightness to washed-out 50% mid-gray for every mobile light-theme user; in dark themes mobile titles render at 50% while the desktop title renders at 80%, so the same element diverges across form factors.

[BUG] The .name replacement copies the adjacent .title rule's 50%/50% pair, silently changing the light-theme value from the original 30%, while the .name rule in common/base/user.scss:123 of this same PR correctly preserves 30%/70%. Light-theme users see the full name in the user profile header fade from 30% to 50% lightness - a light-theme visual change smuggled into a PR whose stated scope is dark themes only - and the .name rule now renders at two different values in different files, so a future edit to one silently drifts from the other.

[BUG] The mobile .name replacement copies the adjacent .title rule's 50%/50% pair, silently changing the light-theme value from the original 30%, while common/base/user.scss:123 preserves the same rule's original 30%/70%. Mobile light-theme users see the profile header full name fade from 30% to 50% lightness - an out-of-scope light-theme change - and the mirrored .name rules in common/base vs mobile/desktop user stylesheets disagree, so the next editor updating one location leaves the others stale.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-maintains the light/dark complement as two literal percentages inside ~90 dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, 100-X%)) call sites instead of wrapping the pattern in one @function that derives the dark lightness as 100% - $l, and the diff itself ships five sites where the hand-typed pair is wrong (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497). Every future theme tweak must redo the 100-X arithmetic by hand at each of ~90 sites, and the next editor who copies a neighboring line - exactly the mistake made five times in this diff, twice swapping the pair outright - inherits or propagates a wrong value; a single 4-line wrapper function deletes the second hand-computed literal at every site and makes the complement structural so the swap/typo class cannot recur.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of this bold link silently changes the accepted value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), producing the exact mirror of the (30%, 70%) argument pair this PR applies to every other 30%-site (common/base/user.scss:124, common/base/topic-post.scss:55, common/base/header.scss:196) — the dark-light-choose call is swapped, not the mechanical dark-theme-only conversion the PR declares. Every light-scheme user (the default) sees this bold nav.post-controls reply-area link washed out at 70% lightness instead of the accepted 30%, while dark schemes receive scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) where the PR's own pattern for a 30%-element yields 70% — so the link renders dimmer than all its siblings in both themes, and the default light theme changes at all despite the objective being dark-theme-only.

[BUG] This .custom-message-length rule's dark-light-choose arguments are reversed relative to its byte-identical desktop copy (desktop/modal.scss:94, converted as (70%, 30%)): the light branch drops the accepted 70% lightness to 30% and the dark branch takes the 70% that belongs on the light side, silently changing light-theme behavior instead of only adding the dark branch. On light color schemes the mobile modal's custom-message-length hint (e.g. the flag modal) switches from subtle 70%-lightness text to heavy near-30% text — a visible regression on the default theme — while dark schemes render scale-color($secondary, 70%), the light branch's value, leaving mobile and desktop showing different colors for the same element in every theme.

[BUG] This h3's light-theme lightness is silently changed from the accepted 20% to 50%, diverging from the desktop copy of the same heading, which this PR converts as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)) at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 — the only 20%-site in the PR whose light value was altered. Light-scheme mobile users see this heading washed out at 50% lightness instead of the accepted 20%, and dark-scheme users get scale-color($secondary, 50%) where the pattern and the desktop file give 80%, so the same heading renders differently on mobile and desktop in both themes with no recorded acceptance of a design change.

[BUG] The profile header .name's light-theme lightness silently changes from the accepted 30% to 50% — byte-identical to the adjacent .title line, consistent with a copy-paste of the title rule — instead of the (30%, 70%) conversion this PR applies to the same .name element at common/base/user.scss:124. Light-scheme users see the profile-page name washed out (30%→50%) with no recorded acceptance of a light-theme design change, and dark schemes get scale-color($secondary, 50%) where the user-card name gets 70%, so the same element now renders at two different contrasts depending on where it appears.

[BUG] The mobile profile header .name's light-theme lightness silently changes from the accepted 30% to 50% — matching the adjacent .title rather than preserving the light value, and diverging from the (30%, 70%) conversion of the same .name element at common/base/user.scss:124 in this same PR. Light-scheme mobile users see the profile-page name washed out (30%→50%) with no recorded acceptance of a design change, and dark schemes get scale-color($secondary, 50%) where the user-card name keeps 70%, so the name element is rendered inconsistently across the profile page and the user card on both mobile and desktop.

[ADVISORY] .custom-message-length is a hand-maintained byte-for-byte duplicate of the rule at desktop/modal.scss:94, and this diff proves the parallel copies drift: after this PR they carry opposite dark-light-choose argument orders for the identical rule. The next color fix applied to one copy silently misses the other — exactly what happened inside this PR, leaving mobile and desktop users with different modal hint colors — and since this rule has no viewport-dependent properties, the duplicate copy exists only to drift; moving it to the common stylesheet would delete one of the two hand-synced sites.

[BUG] This dark-theme-only PR silently rewrites the light-theme value too: the bold link inside nav.post-controls goes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), which is the lightness that belongs in the $secondary branch of the pair. On light themes the bold link in the post-controls meta row renders light grey (70% of $primary) instead of the previous dark grey (30%), washing out deliberately emphasized text, and on dark themes it gets 30% secondary instead of the 70% secondary that the preserve-primary pattern used at every other hunk, so both theme modes ship a value that diverges from the reviewed design.

[BUG] The h3 color drops the original 20% primary in both branches (dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))) while the desktop twin of the same rule at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 preserves 20% primary / 80% secondary. On light themes the mobile h3 heading renders mid-grey instead of the previous near-black, and on dark themes it renders 50% secondary instead of desktop's 80% secondary, so the identical heading rule ships with different emphasis on mobile vs desktop in both theme modes.

[BUG] .custom-message-length inverts both values relative to its replaced line and its desktop twin: primary 30% / secondary 70% instead of the desktop/modal.scss:94 pair of primary 70% / secondary 30%. The modal footer's character-count hint renders near-black instead of light grey on mobile light themes and 70% secondary (far lighter than desktop's 30% secondary) on mobile dark themes, so the same component visibly differs between mobile and desktop in both theme modes.

[ADVISORY] The PR hand-types roughly 70 complementary pairs dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: (100 - X)%)) across 25 stylesheets with no shared helper, even though every pair in the diff obeys the mechanical rule dark = 100 - light. The next contributor editing a theme color must re-derive the complement by hand at each of ~70 call sites, and this PR already demonstrates the failure mode — five sites typed the wrong X on the primary side (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, mobile/modal.scss:102, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497); a single mixin computing the secondary lightness from the primary one deletes the complement arithmetic at every call site and eliminates this drift class.

[BUG] .name's lightness is rewritten from 30% to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent .title rule and departing from the 30%/70% pair kept for .name in common/base/user.scss:124. On light themes the profile header's display name loses its stronger 30%-primary emphasis and renders exactly like .title, and on dark themes it gets 50% secondary instead of the 70% secondary used for the same element in the base stylesheet, so the profile name and user-card name diverge.

[BUG] .name's lightness is rewritten from 30% to 50%, duplicating the adjacent .title value and departing from the 30%/70% pair kept for .name in common/base/user.scss:124. On light themes the mobile profile header name renders at 50% primary instead of the previous 30%, flattening the intended emphasis hierarchy over .title, and on dark themes it gets 50% secondary instead of the 70% secondary used in the base stylesheet, so it no longer matches the user-card name color.

[BUG] The dark-light-choose arguments for the bold author link in the post replies block are inverted: the pre-diff light value (30%) was placed in the dark slot and a new 70% in the light slot, breaking the preserve-the-first-argument convention this diff follows at every one of its other ~100 sites. Light themes render reply author names at 70% gray (roughly 2:1 contrast on white) instead of the previous 30% gray (roughly 9:1), and dark themes render them at scale-color($secondary, 30%) — about 37% lightness on a dark background — recreating exactly the low-contrast dark-theme text this PR was written to eliminate; both theme modes regress instead of only gaining a dark variant.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length dark-light-choose pair is swapped (30% in the light slot, 70% in the dark slot) instead of (70%, 30%), contradicting the conversion this same diff applies to the identical selector in desktop/modal.scss line 94. Mobile light themes render the modal hint in near-black 30% gray instead of the previous subtle 70% gray, dark themes render it in bright 70% $secondary instead of the muted 30%, and the mobile and desktop builds of the same element permanently diverge in opposite directions.

[BUG] The h3 title's light-theme value is silently overwritten from 20% to 50% instead of being preserved, unlike the desktop twin of this same element which this diff converts as 20% to (20%, 80%) at desktop/topic-post.scss line 320, so the change escapes the PR's dark-theme-only scope. Mobile light themes render suggested-topic/link-card titles at 50% gray — now identical to the adjacent h4 byline, erasing the title/byline visual hierarchy and diverging from desktop's 20% — and dark themes get the dimmer 50% $secondary instead of the mirrored 80%, so mobile titles are harder to read than desktop's in both modes.

[BUG] The profile .name light value is overwritten from 30% to 50% (a copy of the adjacent .title rule) instead of being preserved, while this same diff correctly preserves .name at 30% in common/base/user.scss line 124, so the same conceptual element now resolves to different colors depending on stylesheet context. Light-theme profile display names lighten from 30% to 50% gray and become indistinguishable from the 50% .title beside them, yet the user-card .name stays 30% — the same person's name renders differently on the card versus the profile — and dark themes get 50% $secondary instead of the mirrored 70%, dimming profile names relative to card names.

[BUG] The mobile profile .name light value is overwritten from 30% to 50% (a copy of the adjacent .title rule) instead of being preserved, repeating the desktop/user.scss error and contradicting the 30% preservation in common/base/user.scss line 124. Mobile light-theme profile names lighten from 30% to 50% gray and match the adjacent .title instead of standing out, diverging from the 30% user-card .name; dark-theme names render at 50% $secondary rather than the mirrored 70%, so mobile profile names are muted relative to how the same name renders in user cards.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-writes each mirrored dark value as a second literal argument at ~100 separate sites instead of deriving it from the light value, and five sites in this very diff (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497) already violate the preserve-and-mirror transformation, proving the parallel enumeration drifts when maintained by hand. The next contributor editing any of these colors and every reviewer of theme PRs inherits an invariant that exists nowhere as code — the five drift sites above shipped unnoticed; a single helper (e.g. a muted($l) mixin emitting dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100 - $l))) deletes ~100 hand-maintained second arguments and makes slot-swapping and value-overwrite unrepresentable.

[BUG] The dark-light-choose replacement transposes the pair: the rule it replaces is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), but the light-scheme argument is written as 70% and the dark-scheme argument as 30%, the reverse of the 30%/70% pairing this PR applies to every other 30% site (e.g. common/base/user.scss:119). Light themes render this bold link (the username in the embedded-replies rows) at scale-color($primary, 70%) (~#c6c6c6 on white, ~1.6:1 contrast) instead of the previous ~#4f4f4f, and dark themes render scale-color($secondary, 30%) (~#636363 on the ~#222 background) instead of the 70% every parallel replacement uses, so the element is hard to read in both light and dark schemes after a PR whose stated scope is dark-theme-only.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length replacement inverts the pair: the replaced rule uses 70% lightness, but the light-scheme argument becomes 30% and the dark-scheme argument 70% — the mirror image of the desktop/modal.scss:94 replacement of the same rule in this same PR (70%/30%). On mobile, the modal character-count hint in light themes darkens from 70% to 30% lightness (faint gray to near-solid text), while desktop light themes keep 70%, so the identical element renders with opposite prominence on the two layouts after this PR.

[BUG] The h3 replacement uses 50% as the light-scheme lightness although the rule it replaces uses 20%, silently changing light-theme rendering instead of only adding the dark-scheme value, and diverging from the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 which correctly keeps 20%/80%. Mobile small-action headings (suspension/timer/notice titles) in light themes fade from 20% to 50% lightness and become indistinguishable from the h4 line beneath them (also 50%), a light-theme regression a dark-theme PR does not intend and desktop users never see.

[BUG] The .name replacement changes the light-scheme lightness from the replaced rule's 30% to 50%, copying the adjacent .title rule (both now 50%/50%) instead of preserving the original value as every other replacement in this PR does. In light themes the user profile header name fades to the same mid-gray as the title beneath it, erasing the pre-existing 30%-vs-50% hierarchy, and it disagrees with the user-card .name at common/base/user.scss:124 which this same PR sets to 30%/70%, so the same name renders with different prominence in the card versus the profile page.

[BUG] The .name replacement changes the light-scheme lightness from 30% to 50% — duplicating the .title rule directly below it — instead of keeping the replaced rule's 30% as the first dark-light-choose argument. Mobile profile-header names in light themes lose their 30% prominence and render identical to the title beneath them, and no longer match the user-card .name (common/base/user.scss:124, 30%/70%) changed by this same PR.

[ADVISORY] This diff hand-mirrors roughly one hundred dark-light-choose pairs as scale-color($primary, $lightness: N%) / scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-N%), a parallel enumeration a single helper (a faded-color($lightness) function computing the complement) would derive from one number. Every future theme tweak must hand-maintain both mirrored percentages across 100+ sites, and this very diff mis-transcribed five of them (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497), so the next maintainer inherits silently divergent theme pairs that no compile error or test will surface; a helper deletes the second hand-computed argument at every site and makes this class of error unrepresentable.

[BUG] The conversion swaps the intended pair: the pre-diff light value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but this line ships 70% as the light argument paired with 30% as the dark argument, the exact inversion of the 100−X mirror transform applied at every consistent site in this diff. In light themes these bold 0.929em links render at 70% lightness (faint washed-out gray) instead of the previous dark gray, and in dark themes they render at only 30% scaling of $secondary (barely-lifted dark on dark), so the links become near-illegible in both color schemes.

[BUG] Both dark-light-choose arguments are inverted relative to the intended conversion: the pre-diff value was 70% and the identical desktop/modal.scss rule is converted to (70%, 30%) in this same diff, but this line ships (30%, 70%). Mobile users see the custom-message character counter in the flag modal at 30% lightness in light themes (it was 70%) and at 70% scaling of $secondary in dark themes (desktop uses 30%), so the counter diverges from both the pre-change mobile rendering and the desktop counterpart shipped in the same release.

[BUG] The light-theme value of this h3 rule was changed from 20% to 50% by pasting the 50/50 template used pervasively elsewhere, while the parallel desktop/topic-post.scss h3 rule in the same diff correctly keeps (20%, 80%), so the mobile conversion drifted from its desktop twin. Light-theme mobile renders this title at mid-gray (50%) instead of near-black (20%), and the same element now renders with visibly different prominence on desktop vs mobile in light themes — a light-scheme regression from a PR scoped to dark themes.

[BUG] The light-theme argument for the profile-header .name was changed from 30% to 50% (the copy-pasted 50/50 template), altering light-scheme rendering in a PR whose stated scope is dark themes only.
